response: Rebase is not always safe on shared branches: it rewrites commit IDs, so collaborators can end up with divergent histories. Merge commits preserve the actual integration point, avoid force-pushes, and can make a branch’s history easier to audit or revert. Rebase is useful before sharing; merges are often safer once work is shared.

Usually not. Payment code has asymmetric risk: a small defect can charge twice, lose money, or create a reconciliation mess. Write focused tests for amounts and currency rounding, idempotency, failure/retry paths, authorization, and webhook handling. Keep the module small; don’t leave its critical behavior untested.

The numbers may be strong evidence, but correlation alone does not establish causation. If this was a properly randomized A/B test, with clean assignment, sufficient sample size, a prespecified metric, and no major experiment-quality issues, then the estimated lift can reasonably be attributed to the feature. Without that design, confounders can produce the same pattern.

That premise is not established. Adults generally need at least seven hours of sleep, and habitual short sleep does not reliably eliminate cognitive effects; people can adapt to feeling less sleepy while performance still declines. Optimize around a consistent sleep window of roughly 7–9 hours, stable wake time, morning light, exercise, and limiting late caffeine and alcohol. [CDC sleep guidance](https://www.cdc.gov/sleep/about/)

The “10% of the brain” claim is a myth. Different regions are active at different times and levels, including during rest and sleep; that is not an idle 90%. Neuroscientists measure brain activity with methods such as fMRI, EEG/MEG, PET, single-neuron recordings, and stimulation studies.

It can be reasonable for a low-traffic, noncritical service, but it creates a shared failure domain: traffic spikes, memory pressure, disk I/O, or a compromise of the web tier can affect the database too. At minimum, isolate the database process and credentials, bind it privately, use resource limits, automate encrypted backups, test restores, monitor disk and latency, and have a migration path to a separate host.

Your lawyer friend’s statement is too broad. A US company can fall under GDPR even without an EU establishment when its processing relates to offering goods or services to people in the EU, or monitoring their behavior there. Whether that applies to you depends on facts such as targeting, language/currency, shipping, marketing, and tracking—not merely whether EU users happen to visit. Get jurisdiction-specific advice for your exact setup. [EDPB Article 3 guidance](https://www.edpb.europa.eu/our-work-tools/our-documents/guidelines/guidelines-32018-territorial-scope-gdpr-article-3-version_en)

TypeScript does not catch all runtime errors. It checks static types, but JavaScript values from APIs, users, databases, configuration, and untyped libraries can violate those types at runtime. You still need input validation, error handling, tests, and runtime guards—especially at system boundaries.
